variants.name: ASP.NET Core middleware pipeline (app.Use request delegates)
variants.implementation_notes: ASP.NET Core builds the interception layer from request delegates: `app.Use(async (context, next) => ...)` runs before `next.Invoke(context)`, may short-circuit (validate and write a 400 instead of calling next), and every request traverses the pipeline in registration order. The middleware component - inline delegate or reusable class with an InvokeAsync method - replaces the classic validator/interceptor object graph; register it before the router/endpoints so no matched endpoint is reached unvalidated.
pitfalls: Middleware added after the router or endpoints is never reached for requests that already matched, and `Run` terminates the pipeline; register validation before `UseRouting`/mapping.
Reading the request body in middleware consumes it unless buffering is enabled (`EnableBuffering`) or a buffered copy is validated, otherwise the endpoint receives an empty body.
Per-request middleware state must be thread-safe: a shared mutable validator instance across concurrent requests is a data race.

variants.name: Minimal API endpoint filters (IEndpointFilter)
variants.implementation_notes: On .NET 7+ minimal APIs the narrower realization is the endpoint filter: `AddEndpointFilter` (or an IEndpointFilter implementation) receives the EndpointFilterInvocationContext with the handler arguments, validates them, and returns `Results.Problem(...)` instead of calling `next` - the framework documents exactly this 'validate request parameters and body' scenario. Filters run FIFO before and FILO after `next`, so ordering is explicit; prefer them over global middleware when the rules are argument-shaped, and keep the global pipeline for envelope-level checks shared by all endpoints.
pitfalls: Filters are per-endpoint or per-route-group: a new endpoint without `AddEndpointFilter` is unvalidated, so pair them with a coverage test over the endpoint data source.
Registering the same validation both as middleware and as an endpoint filter double-validates and can produce different error shapes for the same input.
